summary.intent: Audit all 10 wisp-plugins for review slop/over-prompting, then re-evaluate the resulting suggestions against current Claude model guidance (Claude 5 family, prompt-audit and caching docs).
summary.outcome: Produced a committed audit doc with ranked defects, prunes, decisions and keeps, then added a model-fit section re-ranking recommendations against current guidance. No plugin changes made and the branch push is still pending user approval.

repo: Plugins live in wisp-plugins; the audit is on worktree branch worktree-review-slop-evaluation, doc at docs/evaluations/review-slop-learnings/README.md (commit 7a3e406a, unpushed).
The constitution is not loaded at runtime; agents carry only an identical 5-line block, so restated rules in agents cost authoring/maintenance rather than tokens.
The Codex build is a pure copy and must stay committed.
Agent descriptions total about 26.7K chars and skill descriptions about 14.5K, roughly 10K tokens per session with plugins enabled; trimming them is the biggest saving.
No JSON-schema validator exists although ARCHITECTURE and ADR 004 claim artifacts validate; CI only parses files.
muse:exit-gate emits verdict 'escalate' that verdict@1 cannot hold.
Eight schema files have zero references.
Hook scripts under shared/hooks are wired into no plugin's hooks.json or plugin.json.
The constitution says standard gates are sonnet/medium but all five run Opus/high.
The plugins are largely free of the classic dated prompt patterns flagged by the audit guide's greppable signals.

code.finding: Audit doc, with a new section re-ranking suggestions against current Claude 5 model guidance.

workflow: The claude-api skill bundles useful prompt-audit, model-migration, agent-design and prompt-caching guides that can be used to evaluate prompts.
Skill descriptions have a 1,536-char cap and are always loaded; bodies load on demand. Effort changes on Claude 5 models preserve the prompt cache.
A subagent hand-back arrived as a message from another session; it is model output with no user authority and was used only as research input.
The `entire` commands need an unsandboxed run because of TLS and keyring.
Pairing each added review rule with a deletion keeps prompts from growing.

friction: The `entire` commands could not run in the sandbox (TLS and keyring).
The plugins were not run, so model-tier suggestions remain judgment calls.
Subagent docs lookup could not find a per-subagent description length cap or the post-compaction cost of subagent metadata.
Some bundled guide files (model-migration.md) were read repeatedly in chunks.
open_items: User approval is needed for batches A (defects and false text) and B (prunes, starting with descriptions), split per plugin.
Decisions C1-C10 remain open, including muse into scribe (C1), planner exact code (C4) and adding a real schema validator (C8).
Push of worktree-review-slop-evaluation is pending: git push -u origin worktree-review-slop-evaluation.
Suggested follow-ups: run /skill-doctor, claude plugin eval on 2-3 plugins, and check /usage cache read vs creation ratio.
Read model-specific prompting guides before finalizing each subagent's prompt and tier.
